Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency and the cost profiling you shared. We want to move the Q1 pilot forward but need to expand the initial capacity and align on a slightly different fee schedule to reflect our burst needs.

Summary of asks: 
- Increase committed GPU-hours in Order Form (initial ramp from 5k -> 12k GPU-hours/month for Jan–Mar).
- Add an implementation SOW line for integration support (40 hours of engineering + 16 hours of QA).
- Provide a short term burst-rate for unpredictable weekends (additional 2k GPU-hours at blended rate).

I've attached a redline of the Order Form (StarHealth_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx) and a draft SOW schedule (SOW_Q1_pilot_timeline.xlsx). Our procurement team needs an estimated delta to monthly fees to take to finance.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 
1) Accept the change as an Order Form change (no MSA amendment) or if legal prefers an amendment to the MSA for the burst clause. 
2) Share a one-page delta that shows the fee impact and any proposed wording for the burst-rate.

If easier, happy to take a quick 30-minute call this week.

Thanks,
Sara Thompson
Head of Partnerships
StarHealth AI

Sara — thanks, appreciate the clear summary. Looping in Karthik (legal lead for order forms) and Laura (sales ops) to scope next steps.

Quick read: 12k committed GPU-hours for the pilot window is doable from a capacity perspective. A couple of notes before we redline back: 
- We typically handle capacity and fee deltas via an Order Form revision (no MSA amendment) unless the change affects a core security/data clause.
- The burst-rate is often implemented as a temporary addendum to the Order Form (exhibit) with a clear start/end date so it doesn't change long-term pricing tiers.

Karthik — can you confirm if the proposed burst wording in the attachment would require an MSA amendment? If not, please prepare a short redline patch we can send to StarHealth legal. Laura — could you draft a fee delta table (monthly incremental cost + one-time integration fee) so Sara has what she needs for finance?

I can jump on a 30-min call Thursday afternoon PST if that helps.

Best,

Marcus / Sara — read the redline. Short answer: we can implement these changes as an Order Form amendment (Order Form v2) plus an exhibit for burst pricing. No change required to core MSA language. Caveats and suggested edits below: 

1) Burst clause: add explicit start/end dates and a hard cap on burst invoicing (e.g., "Burst usage billed up to 2,000 GPU-hours per calendar month at the burst rate; any usage beyond will be billed at the standard overage rate"). This avoids open-ended commitments.

2) Implementation SOW: convert the SOW line into two deliverables (Integration: 40 hours; QA & testing: 16 hours) with acceptance criteria and milestone payments (50% on start; 50% on delivery).

3) Taxes & billing: call out responsibilities for any regional taxes — StarHealth's PO should include tax residency info.

I've attached a lightweight redline (see StarHealth_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx) with inline comments. I'm fine signing off to send this back to StarHealth as "Order Form Amendment v1" pending procurement approval.

If you want to tighten legal exposure further, propose adding a 30-day out clause for the burst exhibit (either party may terminate burst exhibit with 30 days notice).

Sara — once Laura confirms the fee table, I can produce the exact wording you can send to your procurement/legal.

Karthik
Lead Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
